stem: A GP is assessing a child with new strabismus and leukocoria; which finding most strongly suggests underlying intraocular pathology rather than an isolated alignment problem?

options.text: Strabismus can indicate underlying intraocular pathology such as cataract or retinoblastoma
Most childhood strabismus is caused by trauma
Strabismus is only concerning when visual acuity testing is impossible
Strabismus is a reliable sign of infection rather than tumour
Strabismus is expected in all children with bilateral leukocoria

explanation: Strabismus can indicate underlying intraocular pathology such as cataract or retinoblastoma. In a child with leukocoria, this makes an isolated benign alignment problem less likely and should prompt concern for serious ocular disease.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Page 68

optionExplanations.A: Correct because strabismus may be caused by intraocular pathology, including cataract or retinoblastoma, so leukocoria should not be dismissed as a simple alignment issue.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because trauma is not the usual explanation for childhood strabismus in this context.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because strabismus can be concerning even when visual acuity testing is possible, especially if there are signs of underlying pathology.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because the key concern is intraocular pathology such as retinoblastoma, not infection as the main explanation.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because bilateral leukocoria does not make strabismus expected or reassuring.
